clue.text: Military policeman's discussion about east Washington area

indicators.note: the word for discussion goes around the other letters

parts.note: a rap is an informal talk or discussion
E is the compass abbreviation for east
DC, the District of Columbia, is the area of Washington

explanation.surface: A military policeman talks over matters to the east of the US capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition reads as 'is'. A redcap is British slang for a military policeman, from the red cap covers they wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap is the British nickname for a member of the Royal Military Police, after their scarlet headgear.

clue.text: Soldier on line captured in lament with style

indicators.note: the soldier and line are held inside the word for lament

parts.note: an elegy is a mournful poem, a lament
a soldier ant is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A soldier on the line is caught up in a stylish lament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier' suggests GI or a private; here it is a soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something elegantly is to do it gracefully and fashionably, an adverb for with style.

clue.text: Sceptic clearly heartless and not quite nice

indicators.note: with its heart removed, only the outside letters of the word remain
not quite the whole word, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A sceptic is plainly cold-hearted and not entirely pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic doubts the sincerity of others, a close synonym of a sceptic.

clue.text: Guarantee concert is ending in Satie

parts.note: the Proms are a famous series of concerts in London

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A concert is assured of finishing with a piece by Satie.
explanation.definitionFit: A promise is a pledge or assurance, so it means guarantee as noun or verb.

clue.text: Hated sailor worked on plot to nick expensive car

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: to nick is to steal, so the plot work takes the car into itself

parts.note: to work on a garden plot with a hoe is to have hoed it
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, the classic expensive car

explanation.surface: A sailor, tending his garden, steals a luxury car and is loathed for it.
explanation.definitionFit: To abhor something is to loathe it intensely, so the past form matches hated.

clue.text: Sporting superstar landed, losing time

indicators.note: losing means the word gives up a letter

parts.note: alit means came down to land, the past of alight

explanation.surface: A sports star touched down, having lost time.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali, the boxer, was one of the most celebrated athletes of the twentieth century.

clue.text: Displaying heroic style in full? Not in full

parts.note: to be in is to be at home

indicators.note: not given in full means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rich means full, as a rich flavour is full-bodied

explanation.surface: Is it heroic style all the way through? Not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'in full' looks like a riddle, but each phrase has its own job: the first gives two pieces, the second tells you to shorten one.
explanation.definitionFit: Homeric means in the epic manner of Homer's Iliad and Odyssey, grand and heroic.

clue.text: Defensive about curtailed debate — witty character seeing Conservative off

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: curtailed means having its tail, the last letter, cut

parts.note: to argue is to debate

indicators.note: seeing off means getting rid of, so the Conservative letter is removed from the joker word
off, completing 'seeing off', marks the Conservative letter as sent away from the word

parts.note: a card is a joker, a witty character

explanation.surface: A cut-short debate is about a wit who sees off a Tory.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearguard action is a defensive fight to hold off an attack, so the word works as a defensive adjective.

clue.text: Approve turning up after drug treatment

indicators.note: after places the reversed word following the drug

parts.note: E is the slang abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: in a down answer turning up reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: amen is said to approve or agree

explanation.surface: Someone approves a course of treatment after drugs turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a medical procedure flushing liquid into the bowel, a kind of treatment.

clue.text: Seabird heading away from rear of boat

indicators.note: the heading, the first letter, goes away from the word for the boat's rear

parts.note: the stern is the back end of a boat

explanation.surface: A seabird flies off from the back of a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Terns are slender gull-like birds of coasts and oceans, a standard seabird.

clue.text: De Quincey, say, by his own admission, concocted mere Utopia

definitions.text: De Quincey, say, by his own admission

indicators.note: something concocted is made up from mixed ingredients, so these letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: The essayist De Quincey made up a mere Utopia.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas De Quincey wrote 'Confessions of an English Opium-Eater' (1821), so he confessed to being one.
explanation.definitionFit: De Quincey's famous memoir is titled as the confessions of a user of the drug, so he named himself one.

clue.text: A new chapter penned by unassuming boy

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the first letters sit inside the word for unassuming

parts.note: mild means gentle and unassuming

explanation.surface: A modest boy writes a fresh chapter of a story.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-child is an adult who behaves like a boy, or a boy with grown-up qualities.

clue.text: Garment more like culottes than kilt?

definitions.text: Garment more like culottes than kilt?

parts.words: Garment more like culottes than kilt?
parts.note: a garment whose name describes how culottes is spelt with a pair of the same letter where kilt has that letter only once

explanation.surface: Is this garment closer to culottes than a kilt?
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites thinking about trouser legs; the comparison is about spelling: culottes contains TT, kilt one T, so it is DOUBLE T, which is also a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A doublet is a close-fitting jacket worn by men from the fourteenth to seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: Waste disposal expert hurried to take in business meeting

indicators.note: the word for hurried takes the meeting inside it

parts.note: ran is the past of run, to hurry
AGM is an annual general meeting of a company

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off to fit in a company meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A ragman collects and deals in rags and old cloth, a jocular take on disposing of waste.

clue.text: Movement of foot initiating exercises? That's plain

indicators.note: initiating means coming at the start, so the foot movement begins ahead of the exercises

parts.note: a step is one movement of the foot
PE is physical education, school exercises

explanation.surface: A dance step begins a workout routine, and the clue asks if that is plain enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's plain' reads as 'that's obvious', but plain is a noun for flat open land.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland of eastern Europe and Asia, a type of plain.

clue.text: Thieving large amount of money brought about fine expression of anger

indicators.note: brought about means placed around, so the fortune word encloses the fine

parts.note: to make a pile is to make a fortune
F is the pencil abbreviation for fine
rage is a fit of anger

explanation.surface: A fortune paid as a penalty prompts an angry outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilferage is petty theft, the act of pilfering small items, so it names thieving as a noun.

clue.text: Being fond of sex, say, could make nuts ache

indicators.note: the letters could be used to make a different word, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky remark that lust could leave a man's nuts aching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nuts' is slang for testicles in the surface, but it is just anagram fodder here.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchaste means not chaste, not sexually restrained; a fondness for sex is an example of it, hence 'say'.

clue.text: Book probing tragedy, I fancy, finding location of railway tragedy

indicators.note: the book letter probes into the rearranged letters
fancy here means elaborate or rearranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A book investigating a tragedy turns up the site of a rail disaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay Bridge at Dundee collapsed in a storm in December 1879 while a train was crossing, killing all aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tay Bridge in Scotland was the site of the 1879 disaster in which a passenger train fell into the estuary.

clue.text: Republican's second to bellow about First Lady being easily visible?

indicators.note: second picks out the second letter of the word for the party member
the shout goes about, around, the first woman

parts.note: to yell is to bellow
Eve was the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: A Republican's deputy shouts about the President's wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a President's wife, but here it is Eve, the first woman in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed at eye level sits at the height of the viewer's gaze, so it is easily seen.

clue.text: Small trace, say, I picked up on waistcoat

indicators.note: in a down answer on means placed below the waistcoat word

parts.note: vest is the American word for a waistcoat

indicators.note: in a down answer picked up means lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: eg, for example, is what 'say' means

explanation.surface: I find a tiny mark on a waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestige is a small remaining sign or trace of something that once existed.

clue.text: Problem with photography in wine centre?

parts.note: red is a type of wine
the eye of a storm is its centre

explanation.surface: A wine-tasting event has some trouble with its photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: Red-eye is the reddish glare in a subject's pupils caused by camera flash, a common photographic fault.

clue.text: Makes new arrangement of recording in store displays?

indicators.note: in places the recording inside the display word

parts.note: racks are shop display stands
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A record placed on shop stands means repacking.
explanation.definitionFit: To repack is to pack goods again, giving them a new arrangement in their container.

clue.text: Shells old section, but fighter escapes

indicators.note: the fighter gets out, leaving the remaining letters behind

parts.note: former means old, of an earlier time
F is the designation for fighter aircraft, as in the F-16
S is an abbreviation for section, as in legal citations

explanation.surface: Old buildings are shelled, but a fighter plane gets away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ormers are abalones, edible sea molluscs prized in the Channel Islands, known for their ear-shaped shells.

clue.text: Dickens character uncultured after receiving introduction to Gradgrind

indicators.note: the uncultured word, after receiving the letter, holds it inside

parts.note: rude means unrefined or uncultured

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A boorish Dickens figure meets Mr Gradgrind of Hard Times.
explanation.walkthrough: Gradgrind is a Dickens character too, from Hard Times; the answer is Barnaby Rudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is the title character of Dickens's historical novel set in the Gordon Riots.

clue.text: Record reduction in action by mass parasite

parts.note: to tape is to record

indicators.note: reducing the word for action cuts off its last letter

parts.note: work means activity or action
M is the physics symbol for mass

explanation.surface: A record cut in industrial action is achieved by mass protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tapeworm is a flat segmented worm living as a parasite in the gut of animals.

clue.text: Quayside question cut short by bark

indicators.note: cut short means losing the final letter

parts.note: why is a question
arf is a comic rendering of a dog's bark

explanation.surface: A question about the quay is interrupted by a dog barking.
explanation.definitionFit: A wharf is a landing place where ships moor to load and unload, a quayside.

clue.text: Cities laid out on a utopian scale

indicators.note: out, completing 'laid out', means set out afresh, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Cities are being planned on a grand utopian scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid out' reads as town planning; the word 'laid' is part of the letters to rearrange, and 'on a utopian scale' frames the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A utopian scheme aims at a perfect world, which is what an idealistic one dreams of.

clue.text: Sum? Unofficial salesman offloads third

indicators.note: offloading the third means the third letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A ticket tout totals up after selling off a third of his stock.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is an addition sum, as in tot up meaning to add figures together.

clue.text: Political associate's plan — back to front

indicators.note: the back letter of the word for plan is moved to its front

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme

explanation.surface: A politician's assistant has a scheme that goes backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after the definition reads as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is an assistant to a politician or official, so a political associate.

clue.text: Principle is to accommodate blokes in housing

indicators.note: accommodate means house, so the principle word contains the men

parts.note: a tenet is a principle or belief
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: A policy holds that men should be accommodated in homes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a building of flats or rented dwellings, a form of housing.

clue.text: Moderate frequently behind introduction of socialism

indicators.note: behind means the word for frequently comes after the first letter
the introduction of a word is its first letter

parts.note: often means frequently

explanation.surface: A moderate politician often follows when socialism is introduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften something is to temper it or make it less extreme, a verb synonym of moderate.
